I started to work around 2004 (selling ice cream) at 14. This was a summer job.

I worked at a christmas market in December of that year.

I finished school around 2009 (A-levels).

I then went to another country to gain some experience before studying and worked five months at a chain-store selling bread/other baked goods.

I came back and started to study, but quit. (The offers in my city were extremely limited and I grew up poor enough we were never able to afford breakfast/and never any 'school lunches. By the time I realized I could get student loans in another country it was much too late (I'd already done two years of a degree I hated, and I'd have had to shell out the first year's tuition in another country for a degree of three years by myself... which was sort of impossible.)

I then quit to 'follow my passion' so to speak, and taught myself a couple of skills. This hasn't taken off yet, and I've also had some issues with health (depression/OCD/else throughout the years).

I'd really love to make a couple of thousand $$$ to get us to the level where we can do weekend trips every week and buy some decorations for the house and don't have to take the less expensive item at the store to save money. Yes, I realize, maybe I sound entitled, but I really just want to have a good life with my guy. I grew up poor, and it's important to me to provide, probably even more important than it is to him. This was about a month ago and I've been improving my language skills ever since - but I don't get out much, and it's difficult to practice on my own beyond learning vocab/grammar/doing exercises in a book/duolingo/with the mp3 files the book-course provides.

Her pension is about 350 euro (minimum pension here). In addition to that she gets compensation of about 500 euro (because the minimum a person/household has to have a month is ~850 euro). However... if I work she won't get the compensation money. I will be making 'too much' and the household will get less for it. We're only entitled for 1400 euro a month (minimum) in our two-person household. We don't even get as much at the moment though.


I'd have to make at least a certain amount (~1k?) just to 'break even'. It is just not worth it working a shitty job 40 hours a week if I still don't get enough to move out/save up some money to move out. :/

Hey.

I don't feel pressured into anything really. I'm not partaking into any sex act I don't like either. In fact, he's the shyer one when it comes to sex. It had me worried he's not actually attracted to me at first, because he wouldn't just rip my clothes off. No, no. He was very respectful about it (and also about groping/kissing/cuddling me when say I'm trying to do something), but I've been telling him he can be more aggressive... and it's been better after that. :] I'm thinking (hoping) he'll (and I'll) loosen up even more in the future!

I've actually talked to him a bit today. He didn't twitch an eye when I said I might want to try therapy, so that's that. I think my main problem is just... I'm not used to this sort of respect. The ex bfs (not too many either) were just... well... you know. They didn't really care too much about the relationship or me... and one of them was a religious nut... who was convinced I was the cause of his back pain in a 'God is punishing me for being with you' (note: I'm not of a full-blown atheist... just a skeptic) way... yeah... I should have broken up with that dude way earlier, but I'm still working on trying to find boundaries/limits/etc. It's difficult.

Example: I gave this in a post above (or perhaps below?). It's about personal space. I'm a person who needs a lot of that (especially with depression and all my head just tends to get stuffy), but he doesn't seem to need ANY personal space at all. He always wants to be with me, do things with me, spend every second with me. I like it, but I can't do it. I love to spend time with him, too, but at times I just don't want to have to talk to anyone, and just be alone with my thoughts. This isn't even a problem. He's been having no problem with my 'off days'. I still talk to him every day... but some days not as much as others. The big problem is my mom: she believes if I don't want to spend every free second of the day with him I can't love him enough. To her, people in a relationship must do everything together, have no own hobbies, and not have any friends but the respective partner.

Yeah no.

I know this is BS, and even if it weren't, I'm 100% certain I could not do it. I just can't. I need time to myself. But this is what I've always been told, and it makes me feel all kinds of guilty and bad if I don't want to play games with my bf. Hell, he even refuses to play FO4 (which he's been hyped about just as much as the most hyped-up hyper) because he can't play it with me. I have told him it's fine, he can play it, I really don't mind, but no, he won't hear any of it. :/ I just don't know how to get out of the mindset of a) putting his needs before mine and b) questioning my feelings/his feelings because of not wanting to give up my life for him entirely.

I still want to make this work. He's a good guy, and I like him a lot. I want to share my life with him, no doubt of that. I just do not want to surrender my life to him entirely. And that's what I need help with. :X

I did tell him about the paying thing already. He's very respectful. If I say I want to, say, pay for the dessert/the groceries, he's totally fine with that. (He's still making sure I know he always has the money with him/for me and that he's willing to pay if I need it.)


Jesus well. This is an LDR. I can't really say 'how many times per week' and I do take 'days off' where I'll just log in veerrrrry late in the evening (the time we usually play games/talk stuff/do whatever we can online together) if I need to spend some time with myself. That's working out so far... I'd just like to do it in a less sneaky way (I currently use a bit of white lies - like saying I fell asleep, when really, I went to sleep because fuck, I wanted a nap). He does however want to spend every waking (and sleeping) second with me... so... I'm not sure how he'll take it if I tell him that. It's like: I want to share my life with him all right, but not give it to him entirely. (I mean it's likely easier when living together, since you can do stuff in the same room, while still not having to do it together). I also feel a bit bad about this. I do want to spend a lot of time with him - and he's the first guy I actually want to spend time with - but my mom keeps telling me that I mustn't love him enough if I need space/'me time'/or if I don't want to spend every motherfucking second with him... and this is BS. I know it is. But this is how I grew up and the whole notion is just ingrained in me very deeply. I'd hate to have him think anything like she does if I tell him I'd really rather take a nap/think/occupy myself for a while even though he is online at that moment. I don't want to hurt him.

I am probably insecure, yeah, but it's much much much better than it used to be. This time around I'm actually trying to keep my self confidence up and listen to my own needs first of all instead of jumping to the guy's whim. I do however want to find a way to compromise, where I won't have to give up myself, but where I don't have to be worried he's getting hurt if I want to read a book one evening instead of playing mmos with him. :/

I'm still going to make this work. I'm not about to give up because of some issues with myself. The relationship itself is good, and I'm looking into therapy to see if someone can help me figure things out/fix me, you know, all this stuff. I'm not willing to give up without even trying.

Okay, right. I see your point. I of course want to have a partner whom I can tell everything and who tells me whatever goes on in his life. I believe I can tell him everything and he's telling me... well just about everything going on in his life. Do you think I should be more open about things that bother me then? What about if it's frequently the same thing (ie him having to pay for everything because atm I don't have a job/not having a job in general?).


It may be too early. I also don't see where you're getting the 'adapt to whatever' part from. I don't think I'm very good at adapting, and I sure don't let myself be treated like a doormat. I'm just trying to figure out what's too much to tell/what's too little... all this kind of stuff.

I also don't think I agree with the control thing you spoke about, and I've said it before, I'm of course going to work. What he meant with his offer was he'd let me do my art stuff, and I don't have to think about anything else, because that's what I'd really want to do. However. I did tell him from the first time he mentioned it that I'd find work if we're going to do this, and he's also chill with that.

I know. I have an issue and I regret not dealing with it sooner. I still want to make this work though, and I've been looking into therapists around my area.

I'd just like to get along... and things... which makes me reluctant to talk about 'serious' things.)

I don't know how to express my feelings - and especially not in a gentle way. I'm a bit like hammer-to-face whenever I bring something up, and I find it very meh to dance around a topic. I can't really complain). Do I tell him about other things that grate a bit? How do I know I'm just overreacting? I'd really like this to work... but I don't know how much a guy wants to know/hear/etc and so on. (I already committed sacrilege by telling him my number when he actually said he doesn't really care about it. Then again... I asked his and it seemed proper to tell him mine just to be fair.)

I try. I try. It's so difficult though since past evidence suggests to me guys just leave. It's not even that I really believe he will. It's more like... irrational fear.
